title: Oruanui supereruption of Taupō volcano
summary: The Oruanui eruption of Taupō volcano, in the Taupō Volcanic Zone of New Zealand, erupted about 530 km³ of crystal-poor rhyolite plus 3–5 km³ of mafic magma. One study dates it to 25.4 ka and a university science article to about 26,500 years ago, near the end of the last ice age. Researchers call it a supereruption.

uncertainty.note: Two dates in the opened sources: 25.4 ka (Allan et al. 2017) and about 26,500 years ago (Vanderbilt 2019). Converted with year = 1950 - years, an assumption since neither page states its reference year: 26.5 ka = -24550, 25.4 ka = -23450.

importance.justification: A 530 km³ supereruption, the type case of the most recent supereruption studied in detail at Taupō.
